notes:
I wasn't able to research Isaiah 13, so I don't have any notes for you. My first attempt to open eight pages at once (Enduring Word, Precept Austin, Ellicott, Gill, Pulpit, Calvin on Bible Hub, the NET Bible notes and Wesley's notes) went over the tool's usage limit. My next attempt to open just the Enduring Word page was blocked because no more tool calls were allowed this turn.

None of those pages loaded, and your rules say to report only what the pages actually say. So I haven't written anything from memory, and there's nothing I can cite.

**When we continue (next message), I'll go through these in order:**
1. **The traditional reading, verse by verse:** Enduring Word, Precept Austin, and the Ellicott, Gill and Pulpit commentaries on Bible Hub and StudyLight.
2. **Where Protestant traditions differ:** Calvin on Bible Hub or CCEL (Reformed), Wesley's notes on wesley.nnu.edu (Methodist), Spurgeon or Gill (Baptist), and Matthew Henry. The likely points of difference are:
   - whether the "Day of the LORD" (vv. 6–13) refers only to Babylon's fall or also to the end of history;
   - how to read the darkened stars, sun and moon in v. 10;
   - what "My sanctified ones" means in v. 3.
3. **Other views:** the NET Bible notes and Bible Odyssey for modern scholarship (for example, on when the chapter was written and the Medes in v. 17), and New Advent for Catholic readings such as the Church Fathers on Isaiah.

I'll open the pages one at a time to stay under the limit. Just reply "continue" and I'll start.
